texts: hey a doha pls: the cuckoo sings sweet, but keep it with rowdy shrieking birds and it picks up their screech, bad friends ruin you
My quiet cousin started hanging with the boys who smoke behind the school, and in a month his voice and his words turned just as coarse as theirs; he used to sing like a cuckoo.
cuckoo, bad influence
The cuckoo's honeyed voice turns harsh among the shrill; so does a sweet nature sour in the circle of the low.
Please write a doha about how a gentle person, like a cuckoo placed among noisy quarrelsome birds, slowly loses his sweetness and learns their rough speech if he keeps sitting with the wrong crowd.
churn, bad friends
I want a doha that says keeping low company is like adding a few sour drops into a churn full of fresh cream: slowly the whole batch spoils and no amount of stirring will bring back the sweetness.
The churn can bring butter from cream, yet a drop of sourness turns the whole pot; so the base friend curdles the noble heart.
doha: one rotten friend can sour the whole churn of your good habits
After my son started going to the churn-like gossip circles at the tea stall, every wholesome habit of his got stirred up and soured, and I want a doha for him.
yo write a doha, hanging with the wrong people is how nice guys go bad
A doha please for my nephew, who used to be honest and hardworking, but since he fell in with a group of idle gamblers, he lies easily, skips work, and no longer listens to anyone who loves him.
Sit but a season with the crooked and the straightest back begins to bend; write it in two sorrowful lines.
avoid bad company
My best friend used to be so sweet, and then he joined that crowd who cheat in exams; now he cheats and laughs about it, and I miss who he was.

Write a doha about a young man standing at a crossroads, where the bad crowd calls him one way and his parents' advice calls him another, warning that the wrong companions lead one off the path of good.
hey doha idea: you reach the crossroads and your bad friends pull you the wrong way, don't follow
At the crossroads the foolish follow the loudest laughter; ruin waits at the end of a road paved by wicked friends.
When I finished school, the crossroads of my life had two groups waiting: the studious and the rowdy. I chose the rowdy, and I paid for it for years; make a doha of my regret.
crossroads, wrong crowd
Compose a doha explaining that a person of natural fragrance, like the musk deer, begins to lose his worth if he drifts among low company, because the foul smell of others always seeps into him.
doha pls: even a musk deer would stink if it hung with the wrong herd, so ditch those friends
Though the musk deer carries fragrance in its own navel, it forgets it when it roams among the foul; thus the noble soul is lost in low company.
My brother used to be a gentle guy, but his new gang taught him to mock and bully, and the scent of the musk deer in him has all but vanished; could you write a doha?
musk deer, bad influence

My cousin is a bright student, but ever since he started spending evenings with those idle show-offs who drink and gamble, his grades, his manners and even his dreams have fallen apart. Write a doha about that.
bad friends, ruined life
One bitter friendship bends the straight young heart; beware, beware the careless crowd.
pls write a doha warning my little brother about his new friends, they're trouble
I ruined three years of my life following a bunch of friends who never studied; now when I meet any of them I just walk quietly the other way.
Linger with the lowly and you become lowly; the heart is a quiet student of whomever it listens to most.
Back in college I stayed with roommates who partied all night, and by the end of the first year I was the one skipping class and snapping at my mother.
Compose a doha that says even a person with a pure heart will slowly begin to talk, think and behave like the low people he keeps beside him, so one must leave such friends before it is too late.
low company, ruin
doha on how you start acting like the idiots you hang out with
My neighbour's house used to be so peaceful until his son's shady friends started coming by every night; now there's shouting and broken things, and I want a doha about it.
Many a decent house has fallen because the son kept a company the father had warned against; sorrow follows the foolish friend.
house, bad friends
Write me a doha saying that a house that welcomes wrong company, with its entrance open to gamblers and cheats, will see its peace and its honour eaten away, one quiet visit after another.
yo doha: bad friends are like termites in your house, they eat it slowly
My sister is a pearl of a girl, but her new friends buzz around her like bees on a rotten fruit, and I can already see her sweetness being used up; a doha for her, please.
hey could u make a doha: a pearl in the mud stays a pearl for a while, but a bee in a bad flower learns the wrong honey

Please compose a doha showing that even a pearl, if kept among cheap pebbles, is mistaken for a pebble, and that a bee that feeds on bitter flowers gives bitter honey, just as people follow their company.
The pearl shines in the shell, but a bee fed on bitter blooms makes bitter honey; low friends do the same to the pure.
pearl, bee, bad friends
pls a doha: sit with the crow, learn to caw, simple as that
crow, bad friends

Write a doha that says a child of good nature who sits among the crows, loudly cawing and quarrelling, will soon forget his sweet speech and take up their rough manner, so the wise parent keeps him away.
The crow's black voice darkens the whole grove, and the snow-white heart is stained by a black-hearted friend; weave this in two lines.
At the office, a decent guy started eating lunch with the office crow, always gossiping and backbiting, and now he does it too; write a doha for such a fall.
Seek not the company of the wicked, for even the best soul withers in that cold; so sorrow comes to those who love the low.
I used to be honest and now I tell small lies everywhere because I spent two years with friends who thought lying was clever; I want a doha to warn others about how it creeps in.
hey doha: the wrong crowd turned my brother into a liar
It started with just one night out with those guys, then another, and then I stopped answering my mother's calls; I don't even recognise myself anymore.
bad company, bad habits
Write a doha saying that even pure gold, if it sits long among thorns, will be scratched and torn, and likewise a good heart is wounded by the sharp-tongued, and ends up thorny itself.
gold, thorn, bad friends
Gold that lies amid thorns is stained and scratched; so the shining soul among the spiteful is dimmed day by day.
doha pls: gold stuck among thorns still gets scratched, so stay away from bad friends
My friend is such a golden boy, but he sits daily with thorn-tongued friends who mock everyone, and I notice he too has begun to prick people with his words; a doha, please.

I'm a teacher and I see it every year: bright children fall in with the class troublemakers and in a few weeks their whole attitude collapses. Please write a doha for them about avoiding that company.
doha about how toxic friends drag you down plz
I used to run every morning until I started hanging out with guys who sleep till noon; one season later, I can barely get out of bed.
Not at once but day by day the low company eats at the strong will; write it, I beg, in two lines.
toxic friends, avoid
beware wrong friends
doha on the wrong crowd, short and strong, thanks
Though the heart be pure at the start, it grows dark when it walks beside the dark; fear the company of the low.
After I joined my cousin's rowdy circle, the family started to look at me with fear, and I realised my own mother could no longer trust me; maybe a doha will help others avoid this.

I want a doha for my teenage daughter that explains that her new circle of friends who ridicule her studies and laugh at her elders could pull her down, gently but surely, from everything she could be.
yo doha for my friend who keeps hanging out with the wrong guys, he needs to hear it
wicked friends, trouble

Compose a doha that tells the young that bad company does not announce itself with horns, but arrives as a friendly smile, an invitation, a shared laugh, and only later reveals the ruin that it brought.
The unwary one who follows a wicked friend walks blindly toward ruin he never planned; this is the cost of low companionship.
I got caught shoplifting with a group of friends last month, and I wasn't even the one who suggested it; I just went along. Could you write a doha on how bad friends drag us into trouble?
dew, house, bad friends
Compose a doha showing that bad company comes into a house quietly, and the morning dew of its peace evaporates under the heat of quarrels, debts and shame it brings.
The house where I grew up was quiet until my uncle's drinking buddies began visiting, and the morning dew of peace in that house dried up fast; please write a doha.
doha pls: one bad friend visits the house and the peace is gone like dew in the morning heat
As the dew dries at the touch of a scorching breath, so the peace of a house is lost when a wicked friend comes in.
sand, diamond, bad company
Please write a doha showing that a diamond buried in sand cannot show its brilliance, and likewise a person of great talent who keeps low company will have his worth hidden until he leaves them.
hey doha: a diamond stuck in sand loses its shine in the wrong crowd
A diamond lost in sand is taken for a bit of glass; so a pure soul is overlooked when it keeps the company of dust.
My talented friend used to dazzle everyone, but since he started going around with those idle loafers on the beach, he has lost his sparkle in a year, and I wish he'd understand; write a doha.
I turned down a promotion last year because my friends at the bar thought I was getting 'too serious'; now they have all moved on and I'm left with nothing.
I want a doha that tells the young not to be proud of a wide circle of friends if those friends are idle, boastful and quarrelsome, because the size of a crowd matters far less than its heart.
low company
The company of fools is a long night that has no morning for the one who dwells in it; flee before it falls.
doha on avoiding people who drag you down
wrong friends, wrong path
I used to love my morning prayers until my college friends mocked me; I skipped once, then twice, and now I haven't prayed in years, and I want a doha that shows how this happens.
A mocking laugh in a careless circle snuffs out the good habits of the young, quietly, one by one.
doha: bad friends laugh at your good habits until you drop them
Please write a doha saying that the worst harm of bad company is not that it teaches us evil but that it ridicules our goodness until we feel shy of our own virtues and drop them one by one.
My little nephew came back from camp with a foul mouth and a mean streak, and when I asked, he said all the older kids were like that; I want a doha for his parents.
doha for my cousin who fell for the wrong crowd, make it hit hard
falling in with fools
Among the wrong companions the sweetest child learns the bitterest song; keep him far from the low.

Please compose a doha that says a person who is polite and kind may drift into harmful habits within months if his only companions are those who drink, gossip and cheat, because their ways seep slowly through every conversation.
bad influence
Write a doha that tells how a noble person may be led astray, slowly but surely, if he stays long in the circle of the rude and the greedy, so he should prefer solitude over a crowd of bad friends.
doha about how a friend can change for the worse because of other friends
Alas, the gentle soul that stands beside the lowly forgets its gentleness, and its sweetness turns bitter.

I once had a friend who helped me with my homework, but after he began hanging with the older boys, he started laughing at me for being studious. It broke my heart; maybe you can turn this into a doha.
My daughter's best friend looks sweet and polite like a heron on a bank, but she leads my girl into trouble at night; I need a doha about being fooled by looks.
doha pls: a heron sits with the pure and still stays a heron, but a good person among herons forgets how to be good
The heron is white outside but dark within; to sit beside such a friend is to carry shame back with you.
heron, wrong friends
Compose a doha that says a heron looks clean and still but waits only to catch, so do not be impressed by the neat appearance of a companion without seeing whether he drags you into the mud.
I finally stopped replying to the old group chat that only gossiped and mocked others, and within a month I felt lighter, kinder and ashamed of how I used to be; write a doha.
Do not let the worthless sit in the courtyard of your heart; they will not leave without taking something precious.
yo make a doha about cutting off toxic friends before they ruin you
keep distance from bad friends
Write me a doha which says that you do not need an enemy to be destroyed, because bad friends can do the same job quietly, and that the wise person walks away from them before the damage is done.
hey doha idea: stay with rude people and you get pricked like a needle
A needle in a careless hand pricks even the one who holds it; so does the rude friend wound the heart that loves him.
Please write a doha showing that a needle, if held by a rough hand, draws blood, and in the same way a friendship with rude and careless people gives the pure-hearted nothing but wounds.
My grandmother pricked her finger with a needle the day my brother's gambling buddies came visiting, and she said it was an omen; I'd like a doha on such friends.
needle, rough friends
My cousin the weaver used to sit at his loom quietly all day, but then he fell in with some drunk peacock-proud rich boys who left him in debt; please write a doha.
loom, peacock, vain friends
doha plz: showy friends are like peacocks, they look nice but pull you away from your loom, ie your work
The loom weaves fine fabric from patient effort, and the peacock struts in borrowed plumes; woe to the weaver who follows the strutting.

Write a doha saying that a hard-working person at his loom of daily labour should beware the peacocks who strut around him, boasting and showing off, because they pull him from honest work toward vanity and ruin.
I remember how my old friends made me feel like the king of the party, and how quickly they vanished when I lost my job; a doha about that kind of company, please.
sweet poison, bad friends
doha time: bad friends are like free poison, they're sweet at first

Compose a doha explaining that wicked company at first seems sweeter than the kindest advice, and only after much time does one discover what was lost, since the pleasure is brief and the ruin is long.
Honeyed are the words of the low, and yet the honey hides a blade; flee, flee before the cut.
A single drop of sour spoils the pure milk; one wicked friend can turn a stainless life to sorrow.
My sister left a pot of milk near the stove with a spoon of stale curd in it, and by morning the whole pot had spoilt, which made me think of my son's new friends.
Write me a doha that explains how milk, pure and sweet, turns curdled and useless by the smallest spoonful of sourness, and how a noble man is turned sour by the least bit of rotten company.
doha pls: a drop of sour in milk turns it all, same thing with a bad friend
milk, sour, bad company
winnowing fan, wrong friends
doha idea: use the winnowing fan on your friends, keep the grain, toss the husk, bad ones go
Write a doha that tells the wise to take up the winnowing fan and sift their friends carefully, keeping the grain of honest companions and letting the chaff of the flatterers and gamblers blow away.
Take up the winnowing fan, O seeker, and sift your friends; let the chaff of the low be blown far from your threshold.
Last Diwali I sifted rice with a winnowing fan at my mother's and thought, I should do the same with the people around me, the useless ones should go; make that into a doha.
When the wicked touch a gentle one, only ash remains of his good name.
After the party my brother's wild friends left the place covered in ash and ruin, and now I fear for him too, because he follows them everywhere; write a doha.
Compose a doha showing that low company burns the reputation of a noble man until nothing is left but ash, and that even a hint of association brings suspicion upon your whole name.
doha: hang around with the wrong crowd and you end up as ash, quick pls
ash, bad company
a doha pls: a blind man following another blind man will both fall, same for following bad friends
The blind lead the blind to the pit; and he who follows a fool is a fool who sees the ditch too late.
I trusted my friend, who always claimed he knew a shortcut to money, and I lost my savings; he lost his too, and we were both blind to the end, so a doha please.
blind man, wrong guide
Write a doha saying that to follow a foolish or wicked friend is like a blind man trusting another blind man to lead him across a field, and both will end up in the same ditch.
doha: people judge you on the scales by your friends, so don't hang with bad ones
My father, an honest clerk, was suspected of theft only because his best friends were known thieves, and his name has never fully recovered; please write a doha about this.
scales, reputation, bad friends
Write a doha about how the scales of society weigh a man by the company he keeps, so even a righteous man who sits with the wicked is judged as wicked and loses the trust of honest people.
The scales of the world weigh not your heart but your friends; bear the weight of the low and you shall be weighed as low.
Compose a doha that warns the young against the hypocrite who wears a mask of saintly calm and in whose company they slowly become fools and fall into traps that were laid for them quietly.
The neat, quiet-looking man who sits by the pond fooled everyone, including my father, into thinking he was a good friend, a heron in disguise; my father lost his savings. Please write a doha.
Quiet stands the heron on the bank, white as saintliness, and what it waits for is the unguarded heart.
hey a doha pls: heron looks calm, but it's hunting underneath, so do not befriend those with fake calm
heron, false friend
doha on how bad friends corrupt you step by step
Write a doha for the young explaining how wicked companions seldom push you straight to evil but lead you one tiny step at a time, until the evil you once feared looks ordinary.
At first I just watched them play cards, then I held the cards, and then I borrowed money for the cards; I want a doha that warns of such steps.
Step by tiny step the low lead the lofty downward; what shame was yesterday is habit today.
corrupting friends

Compose a doha that says the potter's wet clay takes whatever shape the hands give it, and so does the young heart become what its company makes it, and a moneylender's greed spreads to anyone who works beside him.
doha: moneylender friends and rough potters will shape you wrong, so pick your crowd
The moneylender's son hung around the potter's yard and learned to cheat from the roughest apprentices there, and now the clay of his character is shaped by the wrong hands; please write a doha.
moneylender, potter, bad hands
The potter shapes the clay as he wishes; and the low-born friend, the heart as he wishes; mind whose hands you choose.
Please write a doha for my brother on how every week with the careless drinkers and card players takes more from his health, his money and his name, and how it can all be avoided by leaving now.
It was one night out, they said. Three years later, my marriage is over and my job is gone, and all of those friends vanished at the first sign of trouble; could you make a doha of it?
The company of the low is a slow poison, sweet at first and bitter at the end.
doha pls, since the day i started hanging w those people everything got worse
toxic crowd, regret
They flock to you in spring and flee in winter; such is the loyalty of the low, who love your purse and not you.
bad company, empty pockets
I gave my friend a loan of my father's savings because he swore the money would be returned; the loafers he kept as friends took it all, and now I carry the shame. A doha on this, please.

Compose a doha explaining that the idle and greedy companions are like leeches that attach themselves to a generous man and drain his wealth, his time and his reputation, and then leave when he has nothing left.
doha: bad friends are leeches, they suck out your money and your time
one-string lute, bad company
My uncle, who plays the one-string lute in the village, was a calm man until he began singing bawdy songs with the drinkers in the evening; now he is not the same. Write a doha, please.
The one-string lute is tuned to a single note, but the low companion sings only discord; keep far from his chorus.
doha: even a one-string lute goes out of tune when played in the wrong crowd
Write a doha saying that a soulful singer with his one-string lute will lose the purity of his song if he sings for the wrong audience, because the taste of the crowd becomes the taste of the artist.
lotus, muddy company
doha pls: the lotus is pure but stuck in mud, still stays pure; but we are not lotus so stay away from bad company
The lotus rises clean from the mud, yet who among us is a lotus? Fear the mire, and keep from muddy friends.

Compose a doha that says though the lotus can bloom in the mud untouched, an ordinary human being cannot, and so he should avoid the muddy company of the wicked, who will stain him whether he intends it or not.
My friend, kind as a lotus, started working in a corrupt department, and within a year he lost his clean heart; this is what happens when you keep such colleagues, I think. Write a doha.
Few are the strong who sit with the wicked and are not stained; fewer are the weak who return whole.
I want a doha that says peer pressure is the quiet ruler of the young, that bad friends use laughter, dares and flattery to rule them, and that only the courage to say no can save them from it.
corrupting influence
make me a doha on peer pressure and bad friends, pls
My class monitor, an honest girl, became a bully after joining the tough group for a project; she said she wanted to be liked. A doha, please.
Please write a doha about the heron who stands motionless with seeming holiness while waiting to swallow its prey, warning that companions who look pious may drag us into ruin without our noticing.
My uncle's friend always wore white, spoke softly of God, and borrowed money from everyone, and he vanished before the festival; write a doha on such friends.
heron, hypocrite friend
hey doha pls: don't trust a friend who acts holy, he's a heron waiting to catch you
The heron stands as if in meditation, but its prey knows better; so look not at the guise but at the friend's deeds.
doha pls: a blind man in the forest and a guide who is a crook, that's what bad company is
blind man, forest, bad guide
In the forest of the world the blind trust any voice; beware the guide whose friends are thieves.
Write a doha that says a blind man in a forest is helpless in the hands of a false guide, and likewise a young person who trusts a low companion will be led from the safe path.
My blind uncle relied on a hired guide to take him through the forest path, and one day the guide, in the company of crooks, led him wrong; write a doha about how a bad guide misleads us.
doha: if a blind man befriends a lion it ends badly, so pick your company right

My cousin, naive as ever, befriended the neighbourhood bully who's strong as a lion, thinking it would protect him; the bully now makes him do his bidding, and it is breaking my heart. Please write a doha.
The blind man who sits beside the lion for company thinks it a gentle dog until the lion rises; such is the fate of one who befriends the cruel.
blind man, lion, danger
Write a doha saying that to sit with the cruel without seeing their nature is like a blind man befriending a lion, who will be gentle until he is hungry and then swallow his friend.

My father always said that for every sincere friend in the big ocean of the world there are ten herons waiting to feed on you, and I finally understand him after what happened to me. Please write a doha.
The heron on the ocean shore appears holy while the creatures below tremble; the ocean of the world is full of such friends.
heron, ocean, bad friends
Compose a doha explaining that in the vast ocean of human company there are many hypocritical herons who pose as friends, and a wise man learns to see their true nature before he lets them come near.
a doha pls: the world is an ocean full of herons, don't befriend the wrong ones
cruel crowd, scars
doha: cruel friends make you cruel, plz
Compose a doha about a gentle child who joins a group of cruel friends and slowly learns to laugh at pain, until he forgets he once felt it, showing that company can harden a heart.
A soft heart hardens to the form of the cruel company it keeps, as clay takes the shape of a hard mould.
I was a decent guy until I joined a clique that thought cruelty was funny; now, at thirty, I'm still trying to unlearn what they taught me. I need a doha about it.
doha pls: a blind man's kids hanging w bad friends, under the stars drinking, so tragic
The blind man cannot see his son's company, and the stars above weep over what the night has taken.
A blind man's sons were led away by a group of idle friends who spent all of their father's earnings under the stars, and he knew nothing until the money was gone; write a doha.
blind man, stars, bad sons

Write a doha saying that parents, even those who cannot see clearly, must listen to the company their children keep, because while they sleep under the stars, the wrong friends may be taking everything.
I used to wake with the sun for the morning bell, but since I started staying out at night with my new friends, I miss it every morning; write a doha for me.
doha pls: the bell rings only when struck, and the sun shines for all, but bad friends take without giving
The bell rings for the pure, yet the wicked ring it for gain; though the sun shines on all, it warms not the lowly mind.
Please compose a doha that says even if the sun shines on the wicked and the good alike, the company of the low will keep a person in the dark, and the bell of conscience rings in vain.
bell, sun, bad company
hey doha: befriend a thief and you end up tied by the same rope
Write a doha that warns the young that a thief's friendship is a rope that, once tied around you, drags you to places you never intended to go, so cut it early, before it tightens.
The thief ties the young with a rope of friendship and leads them to ruin, quiet as a whisper.
The thief who lived on our street made friends with my brother, gave him a rope and a plan for his first theft, and now my brother is in the police station; I want a doha about it.
thief, rope, bad friends
A pinch of salt leaves its white stain on the clean sheet; so the smallest low acquaintance leaves its mark on the spotless name.
I wore my mother's clean cloth sheet to a fair, and the salty sweat of the crowd left a crust that never washed out; it reminded me how my friends' bad ways have marked me, so a doha please.
doha pls: salt and a cloth sheet, you put a pinch of salt on a clean sheet and the stain won't leave, same with bad friends
Compose a doha explaining that a clean cloth sheet gets stained by the salt of sweat and tears just as the spotless name of a good man gets marked by even brief association with the wicked.
salt, cloth sheet, stain
ash, bad company
doha: ash is what you get when you let bad friends burn your reputation
Write a doha saying that the ash was once fuel, and that is what remains of a noble man who burned himself out in the company of those who only used him and left him cold.
From the spark of one careless friend, the work of years turns to ash; guard the threshold of your life.
I watched my friend's family business turn to ash because of his lazy, gambling friends, who came every evening to eat and drink; write a doha about it.
I should have listened when my mother said my friends were no good, but I laughed at her; five years later I'm paying for every laugh.
Where the careless sit together, the careless are made; where the wise sit together, the wise are made; choose your seat, O friend.
Please write a doha for the young explaining that every moment spent with a wasteful, mocking and careless crowd is a moment stolen from our future, and that we will pay for that theft with interest.
doha: pick better friends or pay later, lol
avoid wasteful friends
